precepts.text: Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies. You have to hold those children in; you have to take that by the reins. You're the one that's going to form their thoughts, their shapes, their identity. The stuff that Bishop is bringing out, that's not normal behavior, not just for our people, the royalty; that ain't normal period. See how the evil comes up: scripture tell you of idleness cometh much evil. And the part where the eighth head comes in: they know this, and they don't care if it affects some of theirs; that's collateral damage, because they're elite. They're going to make sure that they give theirs those lessons that they need to not fall into this. We the only ones that eat this stuff up.
precepts.point: Deacon: we've allowed mass media to raise our kids, and that's a secondary thing. We've exchanged, and we fell for the trap hook, line, and sinker. Many of our people mistake feeding their kids and making sure they have clothes and a roof and they go to school as raising your kids, and it's two distinct differences.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'

precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” These same kids become the neighborhood oppressors, running around with Glocks and taped-up mags and all that foolishness, and there is no man anywhere in the picture: no man with authority, no dignity, no order, no structure. Ecclesiasticus gives the charge that was missing: “Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies.”

You have to hold those children in. You have to take that by the reins, because you are the one who is going to form their thoughts, their shape and their identity. Don’t give them liberty in their youth, and don’t wink at their follies.

Look at what happens when that is not done. They wanted to kill Julio Foolio over a rap battle: young, dumb, stupid people, wise to do evil. They used a girl’s phone to track him, bought AR-15 type weapons with brass catchers so the shells would not be left at the scene, and shot up his birthday party at a hotel. They thought they got away, but the police got every camera, the house cameras, the phone records, the tag readers and the Flock cameras, and the investigators took their time and put the pieces together. Lock, seal, smack, boom, you’re going down. Your ass is in jail and your mind is still a child. When the enticement wears off, reality seeps back in, and it usually comes with the arrest.

We have children in our nation too, some disrespectful to their parents, some who won’t listen. You don’t know what your parents are trying to save you from, and once you learn it, it may be too late to turn around. That behavior is not normal, not for our people, the royalty, and not period. And the eighth head knows this. They don’t care if it touches some of theirs; that is collateral damage. Their elite make sure their own children get the lessons they need to not fall into it. We are the only ones who eat this stuff up.

precepts.text: Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself. When you die, your son should be in your image. He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness unto his friends: meaning your son will look after your father's friends.
precepts.point: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

precepts.text: Weep bitterly a day or two for the dead, then comfort thyself for thy heaviness, for of heaviness cometh death and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength. Stress makes a man weak: you do not want to work out, you eat more, you gain weight, and eventually it is death. Brothers, do not let stress keep you from the work; some of you have sat in regular clothes for years with the prophecies coming to pass. What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself. The Most High is doing his part; it is time we do ours.
precepts.point: Love thine own soul, comfort thy heart, and remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many. Captain Shamai has pushed working out for five years; a brother lost serious weight only by changing his diet and walking an hour a day around his neighborhood. Walk before you go in the house after a twelve-hour shift, because once you are inside you have more excuses than a crackhead.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.

precepts.text: Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn. That is why the camp teaches God's laws without going left or right; we know we got here through stubbornness.
precepts.point: A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loveth danger shall perish therein. We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come out of Christmas, Valentine's Day and the rest that God never gave us.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshiping the devil, giving gifts to the sea goddess. And we wonder why America is going down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine’s Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. That has nothing to do with us. God did not give that to us.

Sirach shows where stubbornness is dealt with: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.”

That is why we teach God’s laws the way we do. We are not going to the left or to the right with any of you. We are not playing games, because we know why we got over here. We know how we got here: through stubbornness. So if we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

Judges shows how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them”, and “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no leader in place, when the officer, the captain, the deacon or the bishop isn’t there, they go back to their lonesome. If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last.

precepts.text: Remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many; losing Benjamin would have killed Jacob.
precepts.point: Ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave: Jacob never got over Joseph being taken away. Sorrow kills; give not over thy mind to heaviness, for the gladness of the heart is the life of man, and losing Benjamin also would have brought their father to the grave.

note.label: Genesis 44: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and Judah's Surety

precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel. The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days. Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many, and there is no profit therein.”

Sorrow kills. Jacob never got over Joseph being taken away: “Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since.” Of the two sons Rachel bare him, the eleventh and the twelfth, one was gone, and losing Benjamin also would have brought their father to the grave: “ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.” The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and taking the last of it from Jacob would have killed him.

precepts.text: There is no riches above a sound body; do not spend your years on the earth in continual sickness.
precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth. There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart. Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.” Caleb had that sound body at eighty-five, with his strength “for war, both to go out, and to come in.”

Do not spend your years on the earth in continual sickness. Leadership has been pushing that we all need to take care of our bodies and our health. A lot of us deal with gluttony even though it is not a topic we talk about all the time; cut down a little what you eat and eat better food.

precepts.text: Discipline must start in the youth.
precepts.point: Discipline must start in the youth. If you wait until twelve or thirteen to begin, it is over, or you will have a very difficult time.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.” There is a window when chastening still has hope in it, and a father is not to hold back because the child cries.

Ecclesiasticus says the same and says when: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.” Discipline must start in the youth. If you wait until twelve or thirteen to begin, it is over, or you will have a very difficult time; by then he has waxed stubborn and disobedient, and the sorrow comes to your own heart.

Esau has continually tried to take away our ability to rightfully punish our children and bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. The law gives that right to the parent, and it gives it while there is hope.

You may see a different characteristic in my child that they do not show in front of me. You should want other people to see those characteristics that they display. They are a different person around their friends. They are a different person around different genders, and a different person in different elements, different scenes. At school they are this, but in this building they are the perfect soldier. But when it is time to do classwork they do not want to do any of it. But when it is time to be a young man of valor they know all the scriptures, precepts. They are winning awards for doing the commander part, commanding the young men. But when you get them home it is like this dude does not do anything. But they want to go everywhere and ask for everything, and I cannot get you to take out the trash. But as soon as officer such and such asks you to do this, you are the first one there. That is why the accountability has got to be on all of us, to watch all of our children and the different perspectives that they present.

Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart. That wax stubborn goes back to Deuteronomy, to where now he has to be brought to the gates and be euthanized. The gates now, they are not playing with these kids. And they are getting to the point where, no, sixteen, seventeen years old, eleven, twelve, there is a better way to deal with them. We do not have to put them to sleep. We do not have to euthanize them. Sweat equity. We can work them, take their liberty away from them and work them. Had we done that in the beginning, taken their liberty from them instead of allowing them to run wild, and got the sweat equity at home. Do the dishes. Cut the grass. Take out the trash. Read this book. Practice doing this. Watch this YouTube, because I want you to get experience in this. And put them to action.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Chastise thy son, and hold him to labour, lest his lewd behaviour be an offence unto thee. The government would not step in and get the sweat equity. You as a parent are supposed to be getting that sweat equity. You are supposed to teach them how to be adults, because once they are out of your house they have got to do it anyway. At least it can benefit them and their nation.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: He left behind him an avenger against his enemies. When you get older and pass on, the mind of a man is to leave behind an avenger: a kid that finishes fighting the war we were already fighting, that goes out there and wakes up our people and teaches our people who we are according to the scriptures.
We saw that in South Africa: young men out there teaching like young lions, young prophets bringing out the word. That is a crown to a man.

note.label: This Woman's Work

points: Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel: stop overthinking. As Deacon Lahab, a psychologist, put it plainly years ago: you have to tell self to be quiet. When you keep talking to yourself from a place of trauma, you are convincing yourself that the way you have been living is okay. Convince yourself instead that God is right and you were wrong.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days. Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many, and there is no profit therein. Sirach is speaking in what today they would call medical terms.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel. Every class is preparing you: rent, mortgage, food, and gas will go sky-high, up to ten dollars a gallon, and you cannot change it, so why let it weigh your spirit? Stress will kill you. You are your own biggest enemy, more than the white man.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

points: The gladness of the heart is the life of man. Joy brings long life, which is one reason the husband drops dead before the wife: stress and worry wear you to the grave. Brothers who left America say the sickness and the sleepiness after eating went away; this place was created to kill us.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

points: Love thine own soul, comfort thy heart, and remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many. Captain Shamai has pushed working out for five years; a brother lost serious weight only by changing his diet and walking an hour a day around his neighborhood. Walk before you go in the house after a twelve-hour shift, because once you are inside you have more excuses than a crackhead.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

points: Number four: diet and exercise. Diet and exercise will help boost your confidence.

A cheerful and good heart will have a care of his meat and diet. A cheerful and good heart, or a cheerful and good mind, will have a care of his meat and diet. That person will have a care for what they do with their body. The Bible says someone with a cheerful and good heart is a person with high self-esteem, a high standard for themselves.

Someone with a high standard for themselves. You know where that ultimately comes from? Deuteronomy 7:6 tells us that God set us above everybody. So that means our standard has to be above everybody's standard, to be consistent with the word of God. So when we have a high standard for ourselves we are not just going to eat anything. We are not just going to drink anything. We are not just going to let bad things happen to our body and not care about it. We are not going to overeat. Why? Because we have a cheerful and good heart. And that is the fruit of good confidence.

So if you are lacking in confidence, look at your diet, look at your exercise, and see what are some things that you can change to raise your standard. And what will happen is that over a period of time you will look around your life and see where you elevated your standard in many different areas, and now your confidence is higher.

note.label: I Need More Confidence
